transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. Let's get our pre-job huddle going for the annual crane inspection scheduled for Friday. We've got the 25-ton overhead crane in Bay 2 that moves fabricated frames between welding, inspection, and shipping. Right now there are eight finished frames staged in the bay, and four more are expected to come in during the week. Before I finalize any decisions on the inspection plan, I need maintenance, production scheduling, and EHS to review the work plan. So let's hear from each of you — what do we need to consider?

transcript.text: I need to flag something critical before we go any further. During my inspection this morning, the crane brake lining measured only 18% remaining. Our maintenance standard requires immediate removal from service when brake lining is below 20%. This isn't a Friday issue anymore — the crane needs to come out of service now. The repair itself is a 6-hour brake replacement, but after that we also have to perform a 125% rated-capacity proof-load test before the crane can return to service. I haven't entered this in the maintenance system yet, but I'm putting it on the table right now so we can plan around it.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: I need to share something critical for this decision. My confirmed shipping schedule requires exactly 8 frames to be moved to shipping by Thursday at 15:00. The remaining 4 frames can stay in Bay 2 until Monday. I received this confirmation from the customer logistics desk this morning but haven't updated the shared production board yet. So if the crane comes out of service now, we need to figure out how to get those 8 frames to shipping before Thursday afternoon.
